label: refined

reasoning.text: The carried-over material-blending flaw is gone: in the ISO/TOP render the white banks, black ROM, brass multiplier and copper op21 gates now all read distinctly against the blue floorplan plate, and the four grey standoffs in FRONT/SIDE anchor the plate to the die so nothing floats. The two residual defects were (1) the four standoffs at ±1.4 sat inside the 3.4-wide heatsink base and clipped through the fin stack, a visible interpenetration, and (2) the compact_bf_v2 dataflow was under-modelled — the pre-multiplier operand mux, the add-path halving-select mux, and the PWM double-pass feedback all lived only in spec notes, so the exploded datapath under-sold the reference's control structure. Both are now fixed; the silhouette still reads instantly as an HBM-flanked FPGA accelerator card with an exploded logic floorplan.

fields.after: Sequencer driving the 2-bank addressing, the twiddle ROM address (r-counter − 1), the v/B operand muxes and the add-path sel line across the 6-cycle butterfly pipeline.

meta.before: Root everything on the PCB. Populate the board: a gold PCIe edge connector, the FPGA BGA package carrying the exposed silicon die, an in-package HBM stack on each side, a clock oscillator, two bulk decoupling caps and an auxiliary power tap; a brushed-steel heatsink base and fins cap the die. From the four die corners, four thin brushed-steel standoff risers lift an exploded logic-floorplan plate directly above the die; the plate carries the synthesized CFNTT-KRED butterfly datapath (compact_bf_v2). Two conflict-free memory banks (white composite) with their address generators stream u/v coefficients into input DFFs, while a single shared 1023-word twiddle ROM (black composite, storing W = 9^-1·w) feeds the w delay chain. The K-RED modular multiplier is a 4-stage pipeline — ONE 14×14→28 hardware multiplier (brass), then two shift-add fold stages (d = 3z+6q−z>>12; e = 3d+q−d>>12) and one conditional subtraction — producing 9·A·B mod q. A modular_add combines u with the product; two modular_half (op21) copper gates, one on the ROM output and one on the add path, derive the per-stage INTT halving that fixes the reference's 2^10-scaling bug, selected by the NTT/INTT mux. A control FSM sequences the banks, ROM addresses and the sel line; a copper datapath bus threads the stages.
meta.after: Root everything on the PCB. Populate the board: a gold PCIe edge connector, the FPGA BGA package carrying the exposed silicon die, an in-package HBM stack on each side, a clock oscillator, two bulk decoupling caps and an auxiliary power tap; a brushed-steel heatsink base and fins cap the die. From the four die corners, four thin brushed-steel standoff risers (clear of the heatsink footprint) lift an exploded logic-floorplan plate directly above the die; the plate carries the synthesized CFNTT-KRED butterfly datapath (compact_bf_v2). Two conflict-free memory banks (white composite) with their address generators stream u/v coefficients into input DFFs, while a single shared 1023-word twiddle ROM (black composite, storing W = 9^-1·w) feeds the w delay chain. Before the multiplier two selects sit: v_mux picks the A operand (v for NTT, v−u for INTT) and the NTT/INTT mux picks the B operand (W or op21(W)). The K-RED modular multiplier is a 4-stage pipeline — ONE 14×14→28 hardware multiplier (brass), then two shift-add fold stages (d = 3z+6q−z>>12; e = 3d+q−d>>12) and one conditional subtraction — producing 9·A·B mod q. A modular_add combines u with the product; two modular_half (op21) copper gates, one on the ROM output and one on the add path, derive the per-stage INTT halving that fixes the reference's 2^10-scaling bug, with add_mux selecting the halved sum onto the bank writeback during INTT. A copper PWM return bus feeds the K-RED result back into v_mux for the double-pass mode. A control FSM sequences the banks, ROM addresses, both muxes and the sel line; a copper datapath bus threads the stages.

        "english_name": "K-RED NTT FPGA accelerator",
        "summary": "An FPGA accelerator that computes the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) — the polynomial-multiplication core of lattice-based post-quantum cryptography — using the lightweight K-RED modular-reduction scheme instead of full Montgomery/Barrett reduction.",
        "description": "The NTT is a finite-field analogue of the FFT that turns O(n^2) polynomial multiplication in Z_q[x]/(x^n+1) into O(n log n) butterfly passes; it is the throughput bottleneck of schemes like Kyber, NewHope and Dilithium. This design maps a bank of Cooley–Tukey/Gentleman–Sande butterfly processing elements onto the FPGA fabric, streaming coefficients from on-package HBM and reading twiddle factors from a ROM. The distinguishing feature is the K-RED (and K-RED-2x) reduction of Longa & Naehrig: by choosing a modulus q = k·2^m + 1, each partial product is reduced with a couple of shifts, a multiply-by-k and an add rather than a full division, shrinking the critical path and DSP/LUT cost of every butterfly.",
